newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAFRICA TRIBE TAKES PLATINUM WAR TO WORLD AUDIENCE.
newsitem.headline: SAFRICA TRIBE TAKES PLATINUM WAR TO WORLD AUDIENCE.

text.p: South Africa's Bafokeng tribe is taking its battle with Impala Platinum Holdings over mineral rights to new ground by addressing an international conference in Mauritius this month.

"Representatives of the Bafokeng Community in South Africa will address the conference on the need for equitable relationships between mining companies and the owners of mineral reserves," the organisers of the fourth annual Sub-Saharan Oil and Minerals Conference said this week.
The Bafokeng and South Africa's second biggest platinum producer, Implats, have been at loggerheads since 1995.
The tribe is challenging the validity of agreements concluded in 1990 between the erstwhile president of the former Bophutatswana homeland, Lucas Mangope, and Implats.
Under the current agreement the Bafokeng are entitled to 14.9 percent of Implats' taxable income but the tribe says Implats is mining and growing rich from tribal land.
Analysts said that by voicing their dispute in an international forum -- to be attended by more than 35 mining and energy ministers worldwide -- the Bafokeng could gain credibility.
The conference will take place from June 17 to June 19 and is organised by Europe Energy Environment Ltd.
The Bafokeng said last month that litigation to nullify Implats' right to mine tribal land was proceeding.

Implats confirmed on Wednesday that the legal process was underway. "Litigation continues and we can expect a court date to be set for the end of the year to towards the middle of next year," said Implats spokeswoman Ann Dunne.
